policy.note: Asked once on first run (FEAT-001). No design tool holds these screens and the repo (shadcn/ui + tokens) is the design surface; screens are specified code-native in each feature's ui-design.md. Overridable per screen; switch to generate/register by connecting a design-tool MCP and re-running (re-verification registers tool designs after the fact).

SCR-WEB-002.name: Verify Email — Notice
SCR-WEB-002.notes: Arrival (default) state binds to POST /auth/register (201). The Resend control binds to POST /auth/verify/resend (FEAT-002); resend-sent renders the neutral 200. The rate-limited state is reinterpreted by FEAT-002 as a CLIENT-SIDE cooldown (RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS), not a server-throttle response — the resend contract is neutral (technical-design D3/D4), so the UI must not infer throttling from the response. See features/FEAT-002-verify-email/ui-design.md#scr-web-002--verify-email--notice-resend-binding-completed.

corrections: rate-limited state re-bound to a client-side cooldown to conform to FEAT-002's neutral resend contract (no server 429)

SCR-WEB-003.name: Verify Email — Result
SCR-WEB-003.notes: New web route /verify — target of the email verification link (${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/verify?token=…, FEAT-007 forward path). success routes to SCR-WEB-004 (FEAT-003). expired/invalid carry an email recovery form binding POST /auth/verify/resend; invalid folds in the already-verified case (UC-002 exc-3a) per technical-design D2.

SCR-WEB-004.name: Sign In
SCR-WEB-004.notes: Public auth zone, reusing the shared auth layout (centered 400px card + wordmark) from FEAT-001. 'error' folds the four designed login responses: 401 invalid_credentials (generic, no field highlight — no enumeration, FR-AUTH-010), 423 account_locked (FR-AUTH-019), 429 rate_limited (FR-AUTH-018), 400 validation_failed. 'unverified-prompt' is the 403 email_not_verified branch (FR-AUTH-007), reusing FEAT-002's POST /auth/verify/resend + client cooldown. Success (200) sets the session cookie via the web BFF (technical-design D6) and routes into the app-shell SCR-WEB-007.

SCR-WEB-005.name: Forgot Password
SCR-WEB-005.notes: Public auth zone (AuthShell). Served at /reset-password with no ?token=. Response is always the neutral 200 reset_requested; the 'submitted' state shows the same confirmation whether or not the email is registered (FR-AUTH-012, no enumeration). Shares the /reset-password route with SCR-WEB-006 (token-presence switch, ui-design D1).

SCR-WEB-006.name: Reset Password
SCR-WEB-006.notes: Public auth zone (AuthShell). Served at /reset-password?token=… (the worker-fixed reset-email link target). success reflects FR-AUTH-017 (other sessions signed out) and routes to /signin; invalid/expired map 400 token_invalid/token_expired with a 'request a new link' path; field-error is the 400 validation_failed password-policy case with the token NOT consumed (retry-friendly, technical-design D3).

SCR-WEB-007.name: App Shell — sidebar (lists, settings, sign-out)
SCR-WEB-007.notes: Cumulative entry for the app shell, extended once per shell-touching feature; the `source` locator points at the newest and most complete spec, and the earlier ones remain valid for their own parts: FEAT-004 sign-out control (features/FEAT-004-sign-out/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-sign-out-control), FEAT-006 Settings nav item (features/FEAT-006-change-password/ui-design.md, D2), FEAT-009 lists section (current spec). FEAT-009 makes the sidebar the product's primary navigation: one `sidebar-nav-item` per list in `position` order with an activeTaskCount `badge` (hidden at zero — ui-design D2), a per-row `dropdown-menu` (rename / move up / move down / delete, with Delete absent on the default list — D1), and a 'New list' action, all opening SCR-WEB-011. Reorder is menu-driven, not drag-and-drop (D5) — design.md specifies a drag handle only on task-row, and §5 requires the move-up/down keyboard path regardless. FEAT-009 also implements the shell's `< md` full drawer that design.md §3 specified and FEAT-006 §8 recorded as unbuilt (D3), so 'ready' now covers both the desktop sidebar and the mobile drawer. No `empty` state exists by design: FR-LIST-003 guarantees every account has an Inbox. FEAT-010 is the entry's fourth extension: sidebar rows become LINKS to /lists/{id} and gain design.md's `sidebar-nav-item` selected state (primary-subtle bg + primary text + left accent bar, aria-current=page) for the open list, the drawer closes when a row is followed, and the count badge finally moves on its own now that tasks can be created; the `/` placeholder is replaced by SCR-WEB-008 rendering the default list (FEAT-010 technical-design D2). Delta spec: features/FEAT-010-create-task/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension. Lucide icons remain unwired — controls are text/glyph with aria-labels (carried deviation, not an escalation). SCR-WEB-010's UC-004 tag is a likely source typo — no entry created for it. FEAT-011 is the entry's FIFTH extension (delta spec: features/FEAT-011-task-detail/ui-design.md#scr-web-007--app-shell-this-features-extension): the shell gains the DETAIL HOST its inventory entry always described — the `--size-detail-panel-width` (420px) right region SCR-WEB-010 slides into at >=lg, an overlay at md, full-viewport below md, and NOT RENDERED AT ALL when no task is open (no empty gutter). Esc closes it from anywhere in the shell and focus returns to the task-row that opened it (design.md §5). The earlier note that SCR-WEB-010 had no manifest entry is now superseded — FEAT-011 minted it against UC-010; the inventory's UC-004 tag on that screen remains a source typo.

SCR-WEB-008.name: List View

gaps: responsive: design.md §3 specifies a bottom-anchored quick-add below md; this slice keeps the composer under the header at every width (ui-design D5). Owner: FEAT-013 or a foundations pass, once the bottom region's other tenants (undo-snackbar) exist.

corrections: FEAT-011: design.md cited `--color-priority-*`; the real tokens are `--priority-*` — the row uses the real ones and design.md was corrected by the 2026-07-28 amendment.

FEAT-012: `checkbox` specified with `--color-text-muted` (not `--color-border-strong`) for the unchecked ring and `--color-on-primary` (not literal white) for the check glyph — both measured, both proposed back to design.md rather than kept local. See the escalation on this entry.
escalations: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — missing `--color-danger-text` for the overdue chip (3.95:1 against design.md §5's 4.5:1). Filed with SCR-WEB-010, accepted, and landed in tokens.json + design.md; see that entry for the measurement and the amendment.

FILED 2026-07-29 (FEAT-012), RESOLVED 2026-07-29 — accepted and landed as a DOCUMENTATION-ONLY amendment (no token value changed; tokens.json and tokens.generated.css untouched). design.md §2 and §5 gained the control-boundary rule (outline-identified controls use `--color-text-muted` at 4.76:1/6.64:1; components carrying their own text or fill keep `--color-border-strong`) and the muted-text rule (AA on surface/background, not on the sunken tint, with the disabled-control exemption); §4's `checkbox` and `input`/`textarea`/`select` and §8's quick reference now name the corrected tokens; §2's `--color-primary-bright` no longer claims to be the checkbox fill. The product-wide question was ruled on rather than deferred: the line is WCAG 1.4.11's own — is the boundary the identifier? — so shipped form controls are now behind the standard and are tracked as DEF-005 (docs/defects.md), an accessibility pass across the web tier rather than per-feature rework. See design.md §9's amendment log. Original filing, kept because the reasoning is what the next control needs: — design.md's `checkbox` prose fails its own §5 contrast rule, found by the first screen to render the component. Three items, no token value changes: (1) §4's unchecked ring `--color-border-strong` measures 1.48:1 light / 1.64:1 dark against the row surface, below §5's 3:1 for UI graphics — proposed `--color-text-muted` (4.76:1 / 6.64:1); (2) §8's "white check" is light-only — white on the dark `--color-success` (#34D399) is 1.92:1, so the theme-aware `--color-on-primary` is proposed (3.77:1 light / 8.81:1 dark); (3) §2's token table calls `--color-primary-bright` the "checkbox fill", contradicting §4/§8's `--color-success` and unbuildable at AA anyway (2.49:1 with a white glyph) — proposed to drop that usage note. Scope note filed with it: §4 gives `input`/`textarea`/`select` the same `--color-border-strong` outline, so item (1)'s measurement applies product-wide — breadth is ux-foundations' call, not this skill's. Screens are specified against the proposals; blocks no structure, state or binding.

SCR-WEB-008.notes: The product's main working surface, served at /lists/{id} and at / for the caller's default list (technical-design D2) — one component, two routes. `task-row` is realized as a DELIBERATE SUBSET (ui-design D2): title only. The complete-checkbox (FEAT-012), due-date chip and priority dot (FEAT-011), row-click to SCR-WEB-010 (FEAT-011) and drag handle (FEAT-014) are omitted rather than faked — a control that looks live but isn't is worse than an absent one; each later feature ADDS to this row rather than reworking it. The completed section is specified but renders only when non-empty (D3), since nothing can complete a task until FEAT-012. The composer is the empty state's primary action rather than a second button (D4). `loading` is covered by server rendering, not a skeleton — recorded honestly. `not-found` is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's four: /lists/{id} for an unknown OR unowned id gets one uniform in-shell alert, never a disclosure of which (technical-design §3.1). FEAT-011 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-011-task-detail/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): `task-row` gains two of its four deferred parts — the due-date chip (absent entirely when dueAt is null; carries the word 'Overdue' plus the danger treatment when task.isOverdue) and the priority dot (`--priority-*`, with an aria-label; NOT rendered for 'none', since the default state is the absence of a mark). The row also becomes the click target for detail, opening SCR-WEB-010, as design.md's task-row always specified. `quick-add` reaches its full design.md form: two inline affordances opening the SAME due-date-picker and priority-selector the detail panel uses (ui-design D4), each resetting after a successful create, with Enter still creating on title alone so NFR-USE-001's one-field path is unchanged. Still deferred: the complete-checkbox (FEAT-012) and drag handle (FEAT-014). The recorded responsive gap below (mobile bottom-anchored composer) is UNCHANGED by this feature — controls were added inside the composer without moving it. FEAT-012 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-012-complete-reopen/ui-design.md#scr-web-008--list-view-this-features-extension): `task-row` gains the complete-`checkbox` — the THIRD of FEAT-010 D2's four deferrals, leaving only the drag handle (FEAT-014). It is a real <input type=checkbox> so Space toggles complete (design.md §5's own keyboard rule) and it is a SIBLING of the row link, never nested inside it (technical-design D6: an interactive control inside an anchor is invalid markup with undefined activation). Optimistic with rollback on failure (D1): only the box's state is optimistic — the row does not change section until the server confirms, so a failure never yanks a row across a section boundary. The completed section becomes a collapsed <details>/<summary> disclosure carrying its count (FR-TASK-011; technical-design D5) — native, so keyboard operability and the expanded/collapsed announcement come free with zero client JS; still absent entirely when nothing is completed. Completed rows take NO `--color-surface-sunken` hover tint (D3, measured: muted text on that tint is 4.34:1, under §5's 4.5:1 at `body` size). A list whose only tasks are completed is not 'empty' — it shows the collapsed section and suppresses the empty-state block, a composition FEAT-010's spec could not previously reach.

SCR-WEB-010.name: Task Detail
SCR-WEB-010.notes: Minted by FEAT-011 — the screen the inventory has listed since ux-foundations and the 'detail host' SCR-WEB-007 was always specified to have. Route-first (ui-design D1): /tasks/{id} is a real deep-linkable URL, presented as design.md §3's shell detail host — 420px right slide-in at >=lg, overlay at md, full-screen below md. Edits save PER FIELD ON COMMIT with no Save button (D2), which is what technical-design D4's partial PATCH exists for; each control owns its loading/error state and a failed save KEEPS the typed value. Read-only in this slice by design: the status line (complete/reopen is FEAT-012), and the LIST — design.md's task-detail-panel spec lists a `list-picker` but no FR authorizes moving a task between lists and the PATCH contract rejects `listId`, so it is NOT built and is surfaced as a candidate requirements amendment (D3). Priority shows a dot AND a text label (design.md §5: never colour alone). Overdue renders the word 'Overdue', never colour alone, from the server's `isOverdue` — the screen never re-implements the rule. The due-date-picker and priority-selector are shared with SCR-WEB-008's quick-add (D4), built once. Timezone for input interpretation and display is the BROWSER's until FEAT-008 stores one (technical-design D1/§8); the wire is always UTC. `loading` is covered by server rendering, not a skeleton — recorded honestly. `not-found` is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's four: unknown, unowned and soft-deleted ids get one uniform in-shell alert, never a disclosure of which. The inventory's SCR-WEB-010 -> UC-004 tag is a source typo (third artifact to record it); this screen realizes UC-010, with UC-011/012 attaching via FEAT-012/013. FEAT-012 EXTENSION (delta spec: features/FEAT-012-complete-reopen/ui-design.md#scr-web-010--task-detail-this-features-extension): the read-only status line becomes the status CONTROL — the same complete-`checkbox` as the list row, labelled 'Mark complete' / 'Completed <date>', so there is one target and one keyboard path (Space) on both screens. Because one TaskDetail component serves both the intercepted panel and the full-page route (FEAT-011 D1), the control lands in both with no second spec. The overdue chip disappears on completion from the server's `isOverdue`, never a local rule. Still absent: delete (FEAT-013) and the `list-picker` (no FR — FEAT-011 D3, unchanged). At < md the control sits above the fold: completing is this screen's most common action and must not require a scroll.

corrections: design.md §2/§4/§8 cited `--color-priority-*`, which resolves to nothing; the real tokens emitted from tokens.json's `priority` group are `--priority-high|medium|low|none`. The screen uses the real ones and design.md was corrected by the 2026-07-28 amendment.
FEAT-012: the same two measured `checkbox` token substitutions as SCR-WEB-008 — it is the same component (D2, one component, three call sites).

The chip is specified against the amended system.

SCR-WEB-011.name: Create/Edit List
SCR-WEB-011.notes: One dialog screen carrying three UC-008 paths (create, rename, delete-confirm); no route of its own (ui-design D4). Delete uses design.md's `confirm-dialog`, which the system names for 'delete list' by name (NFR-USE-002); the confirmation quantifies the loss from ListSummary.taskCount (technical-design D8) and offers NO undo — list deletion hard-deletes its tasks (technical-design D4). The 409 list_not_deletable branch is rendered but unreachable through the UI, because the Inbox row omits Delete entirely (ui-design D1).

SCR-WEB-014.name: Settings — Security & Account
SCR-WEB-014.notes: Authenticated settings zone (app shell), served at /settings/security; reached from the new sidebar 'Settings' nav item (SCR-WEB-007 entry extended). Pure navigation hub — consumes no endpoint, so no loading/empty/error states apply (not gaps); an unresolved session redirects to /signin server-side (ui-design D4). Renders one list-row today (Change password → SCR-WEB-015); Export data (SCR-WEB-016, FEAT-017) and Delete account (SCR-WEB-017, FEAT-018) add rows to this same entry later.

SCR-WEB-015.name: Change Password
SCR-WEB-015.notes: Authenticated settings zone, served at /settings/security/password — the first guarded form. 'error' covers three server failures on one screen: 400 current_password_invalid on the currentPassword field (UC-006 alt 3a), 400 validation_failed on newPassword (policy, alt 3b), and 429 rate_limited as a form-level alert; typed input is preserved in all three (NFR-REL-004). 'success' keeps the user signed in on the rotated cookie and names the FR-AUTH-017 consequence (other devices signed out) — no bounce to /signin (ui-design D3). 'unauthenticated' is a supplementary state beyond the inventory's three: a 401 on submit routes to /signin (ui-design D4).

SCR-WEB-018.name: First-run / Onboarding
SCR-WEB-018.notes: Not a route: it is the state SCR-WEB-008 renders at / for a brand-new account (ui-design D1). Trigger is explicit so implementation doesn't guess — the caller has EXACTLY ONE list (a single isDefault entry from GET /lists) AND it has no tasks; any other empty list, including the Inbox once a second list exists, gets SCR-WEB-008's generic empty state. First-run is about the account, not the list. On the first successful create it becomes SCR-WEB-008 'populated' — the transition is the onboarding's completion, with nothing to dismiss. Shares SCR-WEB-008's bindings; owns no endpoint.
